core.big_idea: Every person has God-given dignity because humanity bears God's image.

passages.reading_note: Use only for the extension link between God's likeness and speech about people.

core.metanarrative_position: Creation: God gives humanity a distinctive identity and responsibility within the good world.

claims.statement: God made humanity in His image, male and female.
God blessed humanity and entrusted people with responsibility within creation.
Every person has God-given dignity because humanity bears God's image.
Bearing God's image does not mean that God has the same physical body or appearance as a human person.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not use a mirror activity to imply that God physically looks like each child.

core.interpretation_skill: Read what the passage says about identity and distinguish it from physical resemblance.

learning.foundation_objective: State that God made people in His image and that every person has God-given value.
learning.extension_objective: Explain one way the image of God should shape speech, inclusion, or care for another person.
know: God made human beings in His image.
The passage names both male and female.
God gave people responsibility within creation.
understand: Human worth is received from God, not earned by ability, popularity, appearance, or success.
God's image is not a claim that God has an ordinary human body.
practise: Speak about another person with respect.
Include someone who might otherwise be left out.
become: A child who treats people as valuable because they belong to God's created human family.
success_evidence: The child says that people bear God's image.
The child rejects ability or popularity as the basis of human worth.
The child suggests one respectful action.

zero_prep_card.objective: Children say that every person has God-given dignity because people bear God's image.
zero_prep_card.opening: Show two very different everyday objects and ask whether being different makes one worthless.
say: God made people in His image.
The passage names male and female as part of humanity.
Our value does not depend on being the fastest, smartest, strongest, or most popular.
Because people have God-given dignity, we use respectful words and include others.
ask: Does a mistake remove a person's value?
What is one respectful action we can take?
zero_prep_card.do: Read two Dignity Scenario Cards and choose a respectful response.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray: God, thank You for making people in Your image. Help us speak and act with respect.

preparation.passage_context: Genesis 1:26-31 places humanity within the creation account while giving people a distinctive identity and vocation. The text grounds dignity in God's action, not in human performance.
text_observations: The plural “let us” and the phrase “our image” appear in divine speech; the lesson does not use this verse alone to prove a complete doctrine of the Trinity.
Male and female are both included in the image-bearing statement.
interpretation_notes: Avoid defining the image of God only as one human ability, such as intelligence, because that can exclude people with different capacities.
For Kids, the core is simple: God made people with special dignity and responsibility.
James 3:9-10 provides a later canonical application concerning speech about people.
theological_guardrails: Do not turn the lesson into a comparison of children's abilities or bodies.
Do not imply that human beings are divine.
Do not use “made special” to teach self-centred superiority over the rest of creation.

likely_questions.question: Does God look like me?
likely_questions.purpose: Explain that image means a God-given relationship and responsibility, not ordinary physical resemblance.

likely_questions.question: What if someone does something bad?
likely_questions.purpose: A wrong action matters and may need correction, but the person still has God-given dignity.

discussion_questions.question: What does Genesis 1:26-27 say is distinctive about people?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: People are made in God's image.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Notice that male and female are both named.

discussion_questions.question: What responsibility follows in verse 28?
discussion_questions.foundation_prompt: People care for and rule within creation.
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Discuss responsibility rather than domination without limits.

discussion_questions.question: What things do people sometimes wrongly use to decide who matters?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Name performance, appearance, wealth, or power.

discussion_questions.question: How should God-given dignity change one action this week?
discussion_questions.extension_prompt: Name a specific practice and why it fits the passage.

activities.title: Dignity Scenarios
steps: Explain how the response fits the big idea.
activities.learning_link: Applies human dignity to concrete social situations.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Teacher reads scenarios orally and students respond with thumbs up/down before discussing.

activities.title: Worth Is Not a Competition
steps: List three abilities people may have.
Say together: abilities are gifts, not measures of human value.
Name one way different abilities can serve others.
activities.learning_link: Separates dignity from performance while affirming responsibility.
activities.low_resource_alternative: Complete orally without listing individual children.

closing.prayer_prompt: Thank God for people and ask for respectful words and actions.

family.title: Made in God's Image
family.parent_intro: This study grounds human value in God rather than in ability, success, or popularity.

flow.instructions: Use the opening prompt to connect the lesson to ordinary family life.
Read Genesis 1:26-31. Older children may also read James 3:9-10.
Ask what the passage says about who made people and what responsibility follows.
Choose one scenario: someone new, someone embarrassed, or someone left out. Act out a respectful response.
Choose the weekly action, then pray together.

questions: What gives a person value in this lesson?
How can our family show respect in speech this week?

interactive.title: Dignity in Action
interactive.instructions: Take turns completing: “Because people bear God's image, we can...”

family.weekly_action: Choose one person to include, encourage, or speak about more carefully this week.
family.prayer: God, thank You for making people in Your image. Help our family treat each person with dignity.
family.parent_note: Do not pressure a child to disclose bullying or family conflict. General examples are enough.

quiz.question: Who made people?
quiz.explanation: Genesis presents God as humanity's Creator.

quiz.question: What phrase describes humanity in Genesis 1:26-27?
quiz.explanation: The text applies the statement to humanity, male and female.

quiz.question: True or false: A person loses all value after making a mistake.
quiz.explanation: Wrong actions matter, but human dignity is not earned by perfect performance.

quiz.question: Which response best fits the lesson?
quiz.explanation: Inclusion is one concrete way to honour another person's dignity.

puzzle.title: Honour or Harm?
puzzle.instructions: Sort each action into “Honours dignity” or “Harms others.”

printables.title: Dignity Scenario Cards
printables.purpose: Apply the image of God to concrete social choices

accessibility.reading_level: Teacher-read passage with concrete child-facing explanations.
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Explain dignity as “value God gives every person.”
neurodiversity_supports: Give processing time before asking for an answer.
sensory_notes: Children may observe rather than act.

do_not_ask: Do not ask children to name who is bullied, excluded, disabled, or unpopular.
Do not compare bodies, abilities, or family backgrounds.
safeguarding.teacher_response: If a child discloses ongoing harm, listen calmly, do not investigate publicly, and follow the congregation's safeguarding process.
safeguarding.escalation_note: Escalation becomes required if a child discloses abuse, threats, or ongoing unsafe treatment.

editor_notes: Review wording so dignity is not reduced to one cognitive ability.
